items.title: Navalia: Advancing Cowork Agents through Verifiable Task Synthesis and Long-Horizon Post-Training
items.description:
arXiv:2610.26887v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are evolving from conversational assistants into Cowork Agents capable of autonomous planning, tool use, and complex task execution. Financial analysis requires these agents to integrate cross-document evidence and perform multistep numerical reasoning, but expert task authoring is costly, while direct LLM synthesis struggles to produce challenging tasks with reliable answers. We introduce Navalia, a framework for Cowork Agents that combines verifiable task synthesis with long-horizon post-training. Using corporate financial reports as its data source, Navalia semantically selects supporting evidence from complete fact sets and constructs executable computation chains to generate analytical tasks with traceable evidence and actual data dependencies between steps. We further use independent LLM review and programmatic checks to verify evidence consistency and answer correctness. The verified tasks are then used for trajectory collection, cold-start supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL) to improve long-horizon task execution. Navalia, initialized from Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, achieves consistent gains over the base model across all five benchmarks: OfficeQA Pro, FinSearchComp, Finance Agent Benchmark, APEX-Agents-AA, and Workspace-Bench-Lite. These results demonstrate that Navalia improves evidence integration, tool use, and long-horizon task execution capabilities and generalizes to broader Cowork settings, including general office tasks.

_analysis.summary: Navalia提出结合可验证任务合成与长程后训练的协作智能体框架，以企业财报为数据源构建带可追溯证据和真实数据依赖的分析任务，经独立LLM审查与程序化校验后用于轨迹收集、冷启动SFT和强化学习，在五个基准上均优于基座模型。
_analysis.summary_en: Navalia is a framework for Cowork Agents that combines verifiable task synthesis with long-horizon post-training. Using corporate financial reports, it builds analytical tasks with traceable evidence and real data dependencies, verifies them via independent LLM review and programmatic checks, then applies trajectory collection, cold-start SFT, and RL. Initialized from Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, it consistently outperforms the base model on five benchmarks.

items.title: Large language model and reinforcement learning based autonomous construction and progress updates
items.description:
arXiv:2610.26899v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Due to the rapid growth of the global population, traditional construction methods are gradually unable to meet the current housing demand. The advancement of machine learning algorithms has encouraged researchers to explore their applications in the construction industry, leading to more intelligent and efficient building processes. In particular, the rise of large language models in recent years has provided more possibilities for the transformation from traditional construction to smart construction. In this study, a large language model and reinforcement learning based autonomous construction method is proposed. An enhanced soft actor-critic reinforcement learning algorithm is developed to plan actions for a mobile crane according to construction tasks. Robot kinematics and control algorithms are used to ensure that the actions generated by the reinforcement learning algorithm can be executed by the crane. In addition, a customized embedding model is developed to extract information from the construction environment according to user interests. Then, a large language model, ChatGPT 5, is used to update construction progress, provide safety information to control system, and generate construction progress reports. The feasibility of proposed method is verified through several full-scall retaining wall construction experiments.

_analysis.title: 基于大语言模型与强化学习的自主施工与进度更新
_analysis.summary: 该研究提出一种基于大语言模型与强化学习的自主施工方法：用增强型软演员-评论家算法为移动起重机规划施工动作，结合机器人运动学与控制算法保证可执行性；定制嵌入模型按用户兴趣提取施工环境信息；并用ChatGPT 5更新施工进度、向控制系统提供安全信息并生成进度报告，通过挡土墙施工实验验证可行性。
_analysis.summary_en: This study proposes an autonomous construction method combining LLM and reinforcement learning: an enhanced soft actor-critic algorithm plans mobile crane actions for construction tasks, with robot kinematics and control ensuring executability; a customized embedding model extracts environment information by user interest; ChatGPT 5 updates progress, supplies safety information to the control system, and generates progress reports, validated by full-scale retaining wall experiments.

items.title: Pareto-Optimal RTL Code Generation via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Models
items.description:
arXiv:2610.26904v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent studies have proposed reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) methods that enable LLMs to generate high-quality RTL circuits from natural-language specifications. Existing approaches optimize circuit PPA (Power, Performance, Area) by aggregating multiple objectives into a single scalar reward, making it difficult to simultaneously generate diverse Pareto-optimal solutions across different trade-offs such as low power, low latency, and small area. However, in practical design, the relative importance of each objective varies depending on product requirements and design constraints; thus, obtaining a diverse and high-quality candidate set is beneficial in that designers can choose a preferred trade-off a posteriori. In this work, we are the first to propose a learning method for LLM-based circuit generation that optimizes, not the quality of a single circuit, but the quality and diversity of the entire circuit set obtained through multiple generations in the PPA objective space. The proposed method consists of (1) a generation-based training pipeline that reformulates coverage improvement of the entire Pareto solution set into a sequential circuit generation problem, and (2) a reward function based on Hypervolume Contribution (HVC) that measures how much a generated circuit contributes to the Pareto front. Evaluation on the RTLLM v2 benchmark shows that the proposed method achieves +13.3 percentage points in relative Hypervolume over a baseline without PPA optimization and +14.4 percentage points over a single-objective reinforcement learning method, while also demonstrating superiority in circuit diversity.

_analysis.title: 基于多目标强化学习与大语言模型的帕累托最优RTL代码生成
_analysis.summary: 该研究提出首个面向LLM电路生成的多目标强化学习方法，不再优化单个电路质量，而是优化多次生成所得电路集合在PPA目标空间中的质量与多样性。方法包含基于生成的训练流程和基于超体积贡献（HVC）的奖励函数，在RTLLM v2基准上相对超体积较无PPA优化基线提升13.3个百分点，较单目标强化学习提升14.4个百分点，并在电路多样性上表现更优。
_analysis.summary_en: This work proposes the first multi-objective RL method for LLM-based circuit generation that optimizes the quality and diversity of the entire generated circuit set in PPA space, rather than a single circuit. It combines a generation-based training pipeline with a Hypervolume Contribution (HVC) reward. On RTLLM v2, it improves relative Hypervolume by +13.3 points over a no-PPA-optimization baseline and +14.4 points over single-objective RL, with better circuit diversity.

items.title: MedPAO-Assist: Edge-Deployable, Modality-Aware Agentic AI for Radiology Report Structuring
items.description:
arXiv:2610.26913v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The adoption of Large Language Models for radiology report structuring has been largely dominated by either proprietary cloud-based models or large open models requiring high-end GPUs for deployment, which is a critical bottleneck for clinical adoption in radiology workflows that demand data privacy and offline operation. To address this, we present MedPAO-Assist, an edge-deployable agentic framework that generates structured radiology reports directly from radiologist dictation and voice commands, requiring only $\approx3.3$ GB peak RAM and achieving an average end-to-end latency of $\approx31$ seconds on a standard laptop CPU through an asynchronous, multi-threaded execution pipeline. The system currently supports four major imaging modalities -- Chest X-ray, Chest CT, Abdomen CT, and Brain MRI. To our knowledge, it is among the earliest agentic systems to run its entire pipeline with a Small Language Model (SLM) in the 0.6B-parameter range. This multi-agent architecture, built around an Extract-Ground-Generate paradigm, performs concept extraction, SNOMED-CT grounding, and structured report generation, followed by a speech-driven human-in-the-loop correction phase, together forming a fully "no-touch" reporting workflow that requires no keyboard input, external API calls, or internet connectivity. We evaluate each pipeline stage individually -- concept extraction, ontology grounding, and concept categorization and report hardware profiling results demonstrating the system's feasibility for real-time, CPU-only clinical deployment.

_analysis.title: MedPAO-Assist：可边缘部署、模态感知的放射报告结构化智能体AI
_analysis.summary: 提出MedPAO-Assist，一个可边缘部署的多智能体框架，基于0.6B参数小模型，在笔记本CPU上仅需约3.3GB内存、约31秒延迟，即可从放射科医生口述和语音指令生成结构化报告，支持四种影像模态，采用提取-对齐-生成范式，无需联网或外部API。
_analysis.summary_en: MedPAO-Assist is an edge-deployable multi-agent framework built on a 0.6B-parameter small language model that generates structured radiology reports from dictation and voice commands, using ~3.3 GB peak RAM and ~31s latency on a laptop CPU across four imaging modalities, following an Extract-Ground-Generate paradigm with no internet or external API calls.

items.title: DataPraxis: Scaling Analytics Tasks via Verified Workspace Evolution
items.description:
arXiv:2610.26924v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: General-purpose agents are increasingly expected to perform professional analytics work, which requires sustained reasoning, iterative investigation, and reliable evidence. Training these capabilities requires diverse and challenging tasks. However, generating tasks directly from raw data often overlooks deeper questions that emerge through analysis and provides limited evidence for verification. To address these limitations, we introduce DataPraxis, an analytics task synthesis framework based on verified workspace evolution. The framework progressively enriches workspaces with validated findings and artifacts, then inherits and combines these workspaces to uncover deeper questions. It constructs tasks from accumulated findings and their dependencies, verifying analytical results both during evolution and after task assembly. Using this framework, we construct DataPraxis-5K, a dataset of 5,000 verified trajectories spanning diverse domains and output formats, to train DataPraxis-27B and DataPraxis-35B-A3B. DataPraxis-27B achieves 55.11 on DABStep and 51.9 on JobBench, matching or surpassing frontier models such as GLM-5.2. DataPraxis-5K is available at huggingface.co/datasets/stargazerhust/DataPraxis-5k

_analysis.title: DataPraxis：通过经验证的工作区演化扩展分析任务
_analysis.summary: DataPraxis 提出基于经验证工作区演化的分析任务合成框架，通过逐步丰富工作区并继承组合，生成更深入的分析任务，构建了 5000 条经验证轨迹数据集 DataPraxis-5K，训练出的 DataPraxis-27B 在 DABStep 和 JobBench 上匹配或超越前沿模型。
_analysis.summary_en: DataPraxis introduces a verified workspace evolution framework for synthesizing analytics tasks, progressively enriching workspaces with validated findings and inheriting them to uncover deeper questions. It builds DataPraxis-5K, a 5,000-trajectory dataset, and trains DataPraxis-27B, which matches or surpasses frontier models like GLM-5.2 on DABStep and JobBench.

items.title: How Far Can the Gemma 4 Speech Encoder Go Without Changing Its Weights? Saudi and Gulf Arabic Speech Recognition with a Frozen and an Adapter-Augmented Encoder
items.description:
arXiv:2610.28673v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the 305M-parameter audio encoder shared by Gemma 4 and EmbeddingGemma 2 (identical except for its final projection) for Saudi and Gulf Arabic speech recognition, without changing any of its weights. A frozen system trains only a 22.6M-parameter CTC reader over a mix of encoder layers; an adapted system adds 3.1M low-rank adapter parameters, a 41.5M-parameter hybrid CTC/attention reader and joint decoding with a sub-word language model. Against Cohere Transcribe Arabic (2.07B parameters), re-run on identical audio, the frozen system trails in word error rate (WER) but is statistically indistinguishable in character error rate (CER) on five of six human-labelled conditions, while running 3.4 times faster on CPU with greedy decoding. The adapted system is statistically indistinguishable in WER on a public Saudi customer-service call (19.20% against 19.27%) and on clean Emirati speech, is significantly better on telephone-coded Emirati speech, has a significantly lower CER on all six conditions of these sets, and beats a 0.6B recogniser fine-tuned on SADA in WER on all six; it still trails Cohere in WER on long-form Saudi speech. On a blind, human-corrected public call-centre sample it ranks 4 of 15 systems, behind three commercial APIs (significantly only one) and ahead of the other self-hostable systems by point estimate. An optimised joint decoder runs it at 139 times real time on one GPU. We also show that references made by correcting machine drafts favour the drafting system. Code and public-set results are released.

_analysis.title: Gemma 4 语音编码器冻结权重下的沙特与海湾阿拉伯语识别研究
_analysis.summary: 研究 Gemma 4 共享的 3.05 亿参数音频编码器在沙特与海湾阿拉伯语识别中的表现：冻结编码器仅训练 2260 万参数 CTC 读取器，适配器版本增加 310 万低秩参数与混合 CTC/注意力读取器。适配系统在多个测试集上 WER 与商业模型相当或更优，CPU 上快 3.4 倍，单 GPU 达 139 倍实时。
_analysis.summary_en: Studies the 305M-parameter audio encoder shared by Gemma 4 for Saudi and Gulf Arabic ASR without changing its weights. A frozen system trains only a 22.6M CTC reader; an adapted system adds 3.1M low-rank adapters and a hybrid CTC/attention reader. The adapted system matches or beats commercial and fine-tuned baselines on several sets, runs 3.4x faster on CPU, and 139x real time on one GPU.

items.title: Translation and data ethics
items.description:
arXiv:2610.28710v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This chapter introduces data ethics for translation and discusses a number of ethical issues regarding data. These include issues of copyright, ownership and bias, which apply to all types of data, whereas there are further issues particular to minoritised language communities and those on either side of the digital divide, as data is implicated in power imbalances and dynamics. We close with a discussion of responsibility and regulation, and reflect on the growing attention on data ethics from translation studies researchers.

_analysis.title: 翻译与数据伦理
_analysis.summary: 该章节探讨翻译领域的数据伦理，涵盖版权、所有权与偏见等普遍性问题，以及少数语言社群和数字鸿沟两端群体面临的特殊伦理挑战，并讨论责任、监管及翻译研究界对数据伦理日益增长的关注。
_analysis.summary_en: This chapter introduces data ethics for translation, covering copyright, ownership, and bias issues common to all data, plus concerns specific to minoritised language communities and those across the digital divide, closing with responsibility, regulation, and growing attention from translation studies researchers.

items.title: SkillEval: Learning Interpretable Ability Profiles of LLMs via Cognitive Diagnosis Models
items.description:
arXiv:2610.28767v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Current evaluation of LLMs on benchmarks typically aggregates performance over individual examples into a single scalar score. This approach is overly coarse and ignores the diverse scope of skills covered by benchmark datasets. To address this limitation and better exploit benchmark data, we propose SkillEval, a new evaluation framework that performs cross-model, skill-level analysis. The framework integrates advances from two areas: (1) it leverages the meta-cognitive capabilities of LLMs to automatically discover interpretable skills from questions, and (2) it applies cognitive diagnosis models (CDMs) from psychometrics to estimate per-skill abilities of LLMs. We conduct experiments on 3,811 LLMs evaluated on 9,523 items across five benchmarks spanning diverse domains (MATH, BBH, GPQA, MuSR, IFEval). Compared to the traditional average-based evaluation paradigm, SkillEval produces reliable, more calibrated and informative yet concise model profiles that more accurately predict model behavior on unseen items. We also demonstrate the utility of SkillEval in two downstream tasks: (1) LLM routing, which dynamically assigns each query to a capable but efficient model, reducing inference cost by over 60% while achieving improved performance, and (2) Computerized Adaptive Testing (CAT), where an unseen model can be efficiently evaluated using a trained CDM. Furthermore, we show that these skill profiles provide useful insights, for example, how benchmarks share skills and how instruction-tuned models differ from their base models.

_analysis.title: SkillEval：基于认知诊断模型学习LLM可解释能力画像
_analysis.summary: 提出SkillEval评估框架，利用LLM自动发现题目中的可解释技能，并结合心理测量学认知诊断模型（CDM）估计模型各技能水平。在3811个模型、5个基准上验证，生成更校准的能力画像，可提升未见题目预测准确度，并支持LLM路由（降本60%以上）与自适应测试。
_analysis.summary_en: SkillEval is an evaluation framework that uses LLMs to discover interpretable skills from questions and applies psychometric cognitive diagnosis models (CDMs) to estimate per-skill abilities. Tested on 3,811 LLMs across five benchmarks, it yields more calibrated, informative skill profiles that better predict unseen-item behavior and enable LLM routing (over 60% cost reduction) and adaptive testing.

items.title: Scaling Therapy Supervision: Assessing Psychotherapy Fidelity Using Large Language Models
items.description:
arXiv:2610.28772v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Psychotherapy fidelity assessment measures how faithfully a therapist adheres to a treatment protocol, a critical determinant of positive patient outcomes. However, fidelity assessment is bottlenecked by manual expert review, rendering the process labor-intensive and unscalable. To scale therapy supervision and support clinician self-learning, we present an integrated application of large language models (LLMs) that automates psychotherapy fidelity workflows and generates actionable supervisory feedback from authentic, long-form clinical transcripts. We evaluate three open-weight models across multiple task decomposition configurations and reasoning strategies, demonstrating that evidence-first reasoning improves fidelity estimation. Furthermore, we establish the framework's external construct validity on an independent randomized controlled trial (RCT), where it reliably distinguishes Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) from non-CBT sessions across core therapeutic skills. Through a user study that evaluates the generated feedback, mental health experts indicate that the pipeline synthesizes actionable clinical feedback. Ultimately, our work offers a practical, scalable solution toward bridging the community mental health supervision gap.

_analysis.title: 扩展心理治疗督导：用大语言模型评估心理治疗保真度
_analysis.summary: 该研究提出基于大语言模型的集成应用，自动完成心理治疗保真度评估流程，并从真实长程临床转录文本生成可操作的督导反馈。研究比较三种开源模型及多种任务分解与推理策略，发现证据优先推理可提升保真度估计；在独立随机对照试验中验证了外部构念效度，能可靠区分CBT与非CBT会话；专家用户研究认为反馈具有临床可操作性。
_analysis.summary_en: This work presents an integrated LLM application that automates psychotherapy fidelity assessment and generates actionable supervisory feedback from authentic long-form clinical transcripts. Evaluating three open-weight models across task decompositions and reasoning strategies, it shows evidence-first reasoning improves fidelity estimation, establishes external construct validity on an independent RCT by distinguishing CBT from non-CBT sessions, and finds experts rate the generated feedback as clinically actionable.

_article.title: 扩展心理治疗督导：用大语言模型评估心理治疗保真度
_article.summary: 该研究提出基于大语言模型的集成应用，自动完成心理治疗保真度评估流程，并从真实长程临床转录文本生成可操作的督导反馈。研究比较三种开源模型及多种任务分解与推理策略，发现证据优先推理可提升保真度估计；在独立随机对照试验中验证了外部构念效度，能可靠区分CBT与非CBT会话；专家用户研究认为反馈具有临床可操作性。
_article.summary_en: This work presents an integrated LLM application that automates psychotherapy fidelity assessment and generates actionable supervisory feedback from authentic long-form clinical transcripts. Evaluating three open-weight models across task decompositions and reasoning strategies, it shows evidence-first reasoning improves fidelity estimation, establishes external construct validity on an independent RCT by distinguishing CBT from non-CBT sessions, and finds experts rate the generated feedback as clinically actionable.

items.title: Is Anyone Enforcing the Cartel? What Reinforcement Learning Teaches LLM Agents in Markets
items.description:
arXiv:2610.28787v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Evaluations of large language model (LLM) agents report that pricing agents collude at others' expense. Yet collusion is defined by enforcement: a cartel, in which competitors share monopoly profits, holds only if a member who cheats is punished. We introduce an audit that tests enforcement by forcing a member to cheat in counterfactual copies of a market, and use it to study what reinforcement learning (RL) teaches agents in pricing and trading. Small LLMs trained by RL learn what their training rivals reward, but only what they readily try. In self-play, they learn fixed rules ignoring their rivals; against a punishing rival, to be deterred; against a cheating rival, to match its cuts, never the costly price war that would deter it, which they rarely try. A war forced into training is learned, but mostly only where it was forced. Against their own copies, deterred and matching agents can earn the same cartel profits, but only matching ones can enforce them, and then thinly: as a by-product and only against large cuts. Q-learners enforce collusion only in pricing. Prompted LLMs reach cartel-like outcomes mostly through rules that ignore the market. Outcome measures cannot tell these cases apart; the audit can.

_analysis.title: 谁在真正执行卡特尔？强化学习在市场中对LLM智能体的教学启示
